text: {"score":4,"justification":"Numbers match the card: 39.3% of 242 claims vs 10.2% expected, 5.79 risk score, z 5.65, 7 of 13 documented 99215 claims below billed (54%), 4% low-complexity share, 2 of 24 with no lab line. Language is cautious (\"reason to review, not a finding\"), and next steps are concrete and name claims. The cited below-billed claims (C0034797, C0034819, C0034884) are all moderate MDM against 99215, so they support the point. The low-complexity claims (C0034781, C0034821, C0034848) are 99215 with 0-1 conditions, which also fit. Weaknesses: the \"0% for comparison providers\" figure is supported by the card's all_provider_rate of 0.0 for 99215, but the comparison basis is not explained. The note-quality percentages (problems 10%, late 3%, unsigned 0%, data 7%) are not on the visible card and cannot be verified. The low-complexity statistic covers only 4% and shows 4 claims, while the high-complexity table suggests many 99215 claims are on complex patients, and the summary does not acknowledge that. The complexity gradient (49.6% at 5+ conditions vs 15-28% below) is not discussed. The 99215 claims with moderate documented MDM are not tied to total-time criteria (33 and 38 minutes), which could matter for the level, and the summary does not note this. The final step asks for an audit trail, even though the summary says none was received, which is odd but acceptable. Also, \"4% of 99215 claims on patients with 0 or 1 conditions\" is weak evidence by itself and is presented without that context.","problems":["Note-quality percentages (problems 10%, late 3%, data 7%) are not verifiable from the card","Comparison-provider 0% baseline is not explained","Does not acknowledge that most 99215 claims are on high-complexity patients, which weakens the upcoding lean","Time-based support (33-38 minutes) for the cited below-billed claims is not discussed","Next step requests an audit trail after stating none was received, without explaining why it is still requested"]}
